item.title: Alarm settings
item.description:
Sleep as Android gives you complete control over how and when your alarms trigger. You can customize global default settings that apply to all alarms or tweak individual settings for specific alarms (like giving yourself a longer smart wake-up window on weekends).

Accessing Alarm Settings#

  • Global Defaults: Go to Settings ➔ Alarms. Any changes here become the default for newly created alarms.
  • Per-Alarm Settings: Tap on any individual alarm card in your alarm list to customize settings specific to that single alarm.

Per-alarm settings override global defaults! If an option is set directly within a specific alarm, it takes priority over the global settings menu.

item.title: Backup alarm
item.description:
The Backup Alarm is a fail-safe feature that triggers a loud, maximum-volume alarm if you ignore your primary alarm.

This ensures that even if you are an exceptionally heavy sleeper or accidentally sleep through your regular ringtone, you won’t miss your wake-up call.

Menu Path: Settings → Alarms → Backup alarm

Core Options#

Backup Alarm Duration#

Sets how long the backup alarm will ring. Once this duration expires, the alarm will automatically snooze for your default Snooze Time (but never less than 10 minutes).

item.title: Bedtime notification
item.description:
Maintaining a consistent sleep schedule is one of the most effective ways to feel rested and eliminate sleep debt. Bedtime Notifications send you a friendly “Time to go to bed!” reminder so you have enough time to wind down and get ready for sleep.

How to Access Bedtime Notification Settings#

  • Global Default Settings: Go to Settings ➔ Alarms ➔ Bedtime notification.
  • Per-Alarm Settings: Open any individual alarm ➔ Alarm settings ➔ Bedtime notification.

item.title: CAPTCHA
item.description:
If you struggle with oversleeping, hitting snooze on autopilot, or turning off your alarm while half-asleep, CAPTCHAs are your best friend.

A CAPTCHA is a mini-task or puzzle you must solve before your alarm turns off. By engaging your brain or physically moving your body, CAPTCHAs ensure you’re truly awake and ready to start your day.

How to Access CAPTCHA Settings#

  • Global Default CAPTCHA: Go to Settings ➔ Alarms ➔ CAPTCHA.
  • Alarm-Specific CAPTCHA: Open any individual alarm ➔ Alarm settings ➔ CAPTCHA.

You can keep a standard, easy CAPTCHA for your daily routine, but set a more challenging task (like QR/NFC or hard math) for high-stakes mornings like exam or travel days!

item.title: Create alarm
item.description:
Setting up an alarm in Sleep as Android gives you complete control over your wake-up routine—whether you need a simple daily alarm, a quick nap timer, or a highly customized schedule.

Ways to Create a New Alarm#

You can create a new alarm from several places within the app depending on your layout preference:

  • From the Dashboard: Tap the button at the top of the screen on the alarm card.

item.title: Naps
item.description:
Need a quick power-up or a short afternoon rest? The Naps feature lets you set a timer-based alarm that rings after a specific duration (e.g., in 20 minutes) rather than at a specific time of day (e.g., at 2:15 PM).

How Naps Differ from Regular Alarms#

  • Regular Alarm: Scheduled for a fixed time on the clock (e.g., wake up at 7:00 AM).
  • Nap Alarm: Counts down from the moment you set it (e.g., wake up in 15 minutes).

Nap durations can be customized anywhere from 1 minute up to 10 hours.

item.title: Polyphasic sleeping
item.description:
Polyphasic sleep is the practice of sleeping in multiple shorter bursts over a 24-hour period, rather than one long block (monophasic sleep). Because these sessions are shorter and occur throughout the day, they require unique notification and goal settings.

Bedtime Notifications for Naps#

Normally, bedtime notifications are calculated globally based on your main alarm and daily sleep goal. For polyphasic sleepers, each individual nap needs its own specific reminder.

You can override the global defaults for any specific alarm to set a nap-specific duration and notification window.

item.title: Power nap
item.description:
Power Nap is a specialized version of Smart Wake Up. It’s designed for situations where you don’t have a strict wake-up time, but want to ensure you get a minimum amount of rest and wake up feeling refreshed at the end of a sleep cycle.

How it Works#

Instead of setting a specific alarm time, you set a minimum duration and a smart period. The app ensures you sleep for at least that minimum time, and then looks for the best moment to wake you up during the following smart period.

item.title: Snooze
item.description:
We all have those mornings when we just need a few extra minutes in bed. Snoozing lets you temporarily delay your wake-up, but to make sure you don’t accidentally oversleep, we also offer a variety of helpful limits.

Where to Configure Snoozes#

  • Global Default: Set your baseline snooze duration and limits for all new alarms by navigating to Settings → Alarms → Snooze.
  • Individual Alarms: Override the default snooze behavior for a specific alarm in its Per-alarm settings → Snooze.

Example: If your alarm goes off at 5:30 AM, and you wake up after a while at 5:33 AM but decide you need a bit more rest, you can hit the 10-minute snooze button. Your alarm will pause and gently wake you again at 5:43 AM (5:33 + 10 minutes).

item.title: Sound
item.description:
Wake up your way! Sleep as Android lets you choose from built-in nature sounds, local audio files, online radio stations, or streaming platforms like Spotify to make your mornings as pleasant or energizing as you need.

Where to Configure Sounds#

  • Global Default: Set your baseline sound for all new alarms by navigating to Settings ➔ Alarms ➔ Sound.
  • Individual Alarms: Override the default sound for a specific alarm in its Per-alarm settings ➔ Sound.

Nature Sounds#

Enjoy a curated library of calming, high-quality nature sounds designed for a peaceful wake-up experience (e.g., birdsong, ocean waves, gentle rain, storms).
